questions.q: Was concealing the buyer behind a one-month-old LLC ordinary for this auction, and who else bid?
questions.known: San Rafael Ranch LLC was registered roughly a month before the purchase and the owners' names were withheld. The concealment broke only via a street-name change and a tax contest, i.e. by accident rather than disclosure.
questions.who: The auction house · the Epstein estate's compensation administrators · NM Secretary of State
questions.doc: Auction records; the LLC's formation filing; the recorded warranty deed
questions.next: Not scheduled — requires a records request
questions.status: Open · not being pursued by anyone visible

questions.q: What evidentiary value was lost at the site between 2019 and the state regaining access in 2026?
questions.known: The property changed hands at auction in 2023, was renamed, and unpermitted construction began. Investigators reported excavation and altered substrate inconsistent with the original construction timeline. The state did not have investigative access during that period.
questions.who: NMDOJ investigators · Santa Fe County permitting · the current owners
questions.doc: The stop-work order and permit file; the state's search inventory from March 2026
questions.next: The New Mexico truth commission's subpoena returns

questions.q: Did the Justice Department revisit its stand-down request after 10 August 2019, when the stated rationale for it — the risk of parallel prosecutions — ceased to exist?
questions.known: The stated reason for asking New Mexico to stand down in July 2019 was the risk that parallel investigations would generate inconsistent statements. The federal defendant died on 10 August 2019, roughly two and a half weeks later, ending that prosecution. New Mexico alleges the promised information was never provided and is litigating for it in 2026 — six and a half years later.
questions.who: The Justice Department · the SDNY prosecutors of record in 2019 · Todd Blanche
questions.doc: Any internal DOJ review of the 2019 referral commitment; the government's answer to the New Mexico complaint
questions.next: The government's response on the D.D.C. docket

contradictions.asrc: Federal rationale for the stand-down request, July 2019
contradictions.b: The federal prosecution ended on 10 August 2019, and the material was still withheld in 2026
contradictions.st: Unreconciled. The stated reason expired roughly 18 days after it was given; the withholding outlasted it by more than six years.
